Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
322 AM EDT Fri Sep 4 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 322 AM EDT Friday...

No significant changes have been made to the forecast at this time.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 322 AM EDT Friday...

1. Showers possible today and Saturday with drier weather 
expected Sunday and Monday.

2. Several rounds of showers will be possible next week, but no 
significant weather is expected. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 322 AM EDT Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: An upper level low will be anchored to our northeast 
today with a weak shortwave moving through the longwave trough. This 
energy is expected to spark isolated showers this afternoon but the 
lack of any appreciable instability or moisture will keep the areal 
coverage low and the intensity light. We will see an increase in 
shower activity across the region on Saturday as a second shortwave 
helps to deepen the low to our northeast and the low sinks to the 
southeast. This will increase mid-level lift while increasing mid-
level lapse rates and therefore slightly increase instability. With 
east/northeast winds in the low to mid levels, we should advect in 
some Atlantic moisture which will also aid in increasing the areal 
coverage of showers. However, precipitation rates will remain meager 
with just some periodic light rain throughout the day on Saturday. 
Deep layer ridging will build overhead on Sunday and continue into 
Monday which will keep seasonably cool temperatures in the forecast 
while also bringing plentiful sunshine and dry weather.

KEY MESSAGE 2: After a seasonable and dry holiday weekend, chances for 
showers look to return throughout next week, although no significant 
weather is expected at this time. Starting with Monday night into 
Tuesday, a cold front looks to push across the region driving shower 
activity, although rainfall will be limited given lack of deep 
moisture. As the week progresses, several shortwaves look to move 
through, bringing chances for light rain showers each day, with 
Thursday possibly seeing the most coverage. Despite the chances for 
showers, no day looks to be a complete washout at this time given 
the showery nature of the precipitation, but an extended period of 
dry weather is not expected either. Temperatures for next week look 
to be on the cool side for the most part, with high temperatures in 
the upper 60s and 70s through the week and overnight lows in the 40s 
and 50s.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Through 06Z Saturday...Main concern for aviation throughout the
forecast period will be developing fog and mist across the region
tonight with a mix of flight conditions expected across terminals.
The greatest confidence for fog continues to be at KSLK and KMSS
where it is currently occurring, followed by KEFK and KMPV. 
Given the uncertainty, a mix of TEMPO and prevailing groups were
utilized in the TAF. Any lingering fog should dissipate towards
13Z. Winds will remain calm overnight before northwest winds 
increase through the morning, generally 5 to 10 knots with a few
gust 15 to 20 knots possible through the afternoon. A few 
scattered showers are expected to develop throughout the 
afternoon, but there is low confidence any showers impacting any
terminals at this point, so have left mention out of the 
forecast for now.

Outlook...

Saturday: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA,
